items.title: Rental Renovation Licensing By-law, COR-2026-045, listed at item 7.2.i.
notes:
Council considered the Rental Renovation Licensing By-law, COR‑2026‑045, listed as Item 7.2.i. on today’s agenda. Council also received written submissions from Sarah Molnar, JT Macleod, Leslie Macredie, Ken Vogelpohl and Jacquie Wells (ACORN), Kayla Andrade, Mary Ann Fleming Millar, Jennifer Roswell, Greg Quinnell, Peggy Nickels, Barbara Smith, Magdalena Milosz, Darlene Rehman, and Lori Landford.

Kristin VanDerGeld, Manager, Licensing and Natalie Goss, Manager, Policy and Research, were in attendance to respond to questions from Council.

Hafeez Hussain, Sarah Molnar, and Marshal Sandu addressed Council in opposition to the proposed Rental Renovation Licensing By-law. The delegations cited concerns regarding additional restrictions that may deter property owners from becoming small‑scale landlords; concerns about municipal jurisdiction and duplication of provincial law; and concerns about rising financial costs for small‑scale landlords.

Barbara Smith, Douglas Kwan, Rachel Whitney, Ken Vogelpohl, and Jacquie Wells addressed Council in support of the Rental Renovation Licensing By-law. Several delegations shared the following reasons for their support: references to sections of the Municipal Act that support the City’s jurisdiction to approve such a by-law; concerns about misinformation regarding profit margins for small landlords and the financial burden they face; the belief that the by-law will help mitigate bad‑faith evictions; and the by-law’s alignment with the City’s Housing for All Strategy. It was also noted that there are ongoing concerns about the lack of consequences for landlords who evict in bad faith. Ken Vogelpohl and Jacquie Wells further stated that since the initial committee meeting, the City of Mississauga has passed a rental renoviction licensing by-law that includes tenant compensation, adding to the number of municipalities pursuing similar measures.

Kayla Andrade, Ontario Landlords Watch, spoke in opposition to the Rental Renovation Licensing By-law. Ms. Andrade discussed the Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB), the volume of cases it handles, existing tenant protections, and current tenant rights and challenges. She noted that several of these issues may discourage individuals from investing in the City. Ms. Andrade then responded to questions from Council.

Ron Druckenmill and Sid MacDonald spoke in support of implementing a Rental Renovation Licensing By-law. They further requested that Council approve the proposed amendment allowing for tenant moving compensation.

Paul Margani spoke in opposition to the proposed by-law. Mr. Margani raised concerns about the LTB and its operational procedures, noting that if a review of the LTB were completed, the proposed by-law might not be necessary. He further advised that fairness between landlords and tenants is essential, and that collaboration between the groups could shift the focus toward addressing issues within the LTB.

Jordan Morelli, Moe Hansrod, Diane Digiandomenico, Kory MacKinnon, Kyla Shaw, Michael Richter, and Danielle Chiasson spoke in opposition to the proposed by-law. Concerns included provincial downloading, issues with the LTB process, potential added pressures and restrictions on landlords, inflation-related challenges, and the potential precedent set by other municipalities adopting similar by-laws.

Peggy Nickels addressed Council in support of the rental renoviction by-law.

Kourtney Payne‑Short stated that, as a landlord, she supports the proposed by-law.

Peter Eglin addressed Council in support of the proposed by-law.

items.title: Rental Renovation Licensing By-law, COR-2026-045, listed at item 7.2.i. (Cont'd)
notes:
In response to questions, K. VanDerGeld stated there was no legislation preventing this by-law from being approved. 

Questions were raised regarding the Budget, J. Lautenbach advised that the proposed program is a best estimate to date on the financial impacts to the tax levy. J. Lautenbach stated that there could be additional costs beyond those outlined in the report, the full costs of the program are unknown to date. In response to further questions, Dimetra Resendes, Acting General Manager, Corporate Services, advised in 2025 staff brought forward a report on this matter and at that time staff did not recommend pursuing a By-law, it was recommended that additional education be proposed, it was only as a result of Council direction that resulted in the staff recommendation this date, noting the staff recommendation is an increase in service delivery.

Councillor S. Davey questioned the potential impacts of the 2027 budget. J. Lautenbach stated this year could be a challenging budget year. 

Councillor D. Chapman question whether staff had an opportunity to review the reserve funds to help to offsets the costs of the additional FTE's. J. Lautenbach noted while there may be a variance for 2026, reserve funds cannot be a permanent solution to funding FTE's in the future.  In response to questions, J. Lautenbach advised that this program may result in an annual increase of $15 on the average home owner.

In response to questions, K. VanDerGeld provided a response on the number of N13's that were filed with the landlord tenanted board in the following years.

Councillors P. Singh and S. Stretch left the meeting at this time.

A motion was brought forward by Councillor S. Davey, seconded by Councillor B. Ioannidis to approve the recommendation as outlined in COR-2026-045.

Councillor D. Chapman brought forward a motion to amend the proposed implementation timeline to September 1, 2026, rather than January 1, 2027, the amendment failed to receive a seconder.

Councillor D. Chapman brought forward a further amendment, which was included in the agenda this date, related to tenant compensation, which was seconded by Councillor C. Michaud. 

Councillor J. Deneault brought forward motion to amend the moving cost allocation to

a) $250.00 for a Rental Unit with up to one (1) bedroom; or
b) $500.00 for a Rental Unit with two (2) or more bedrooms.

rather than the proposed $1000., which was seconded by Councillor C. Michaud.

Councillor S. Davey brought forward a motion to defer consideration on the motion to the 2027 budget process, which was seconded by Councillor D. Schnider

Councillor Davey's deferral motion was then voted on and was LOST on a recorded vote, with Councillors S. Davey, D. Schnider, B. Ioannidis and A. Owodunni voting in favour; and, Mayor B. Vrbanovic and Councillors D. Chapman, C. Michaud, J. Deneault and M. Johnston voting in opposition.

Councillor J. Deneault's amendment was then voted on and was Carried on a recorded vote, with Mayor B. Vrbanovic and Councillors A. Owodunni, S. Davey, M. Johnston, C. Michaud, D. Schnider and J. Deneault voting in favour; and, Councillors B. Ioannidis and D. Chapman voting in opposition.

Councillor D. Chapman's amendment was then voted on and was LOST on a recorded vote, with Mayor B. Vrbanovic and Councillors D. Chapman, J. Deneault, M. Johnston voting in favour; and, Councillors S. Davey, D. Schnider, B. Ioannidis, A. Owodunni and C. Michaud voting in opposition.

- MAYORAL BUSINESS AND UPDATES - MAYOR B. VRBANOVIC
notes:
Mayor B. Vrbanovic provided an update from the Region of Waterloo on the Mannheim Service Area water capacity constraint. He noted that on April 1, 2026, the Region informed area municipalities that new or expanded pre‑schools, elementary and secondary schools, daycare centres, and religious institutions within the Mannheim Service Area may now proceed through the normal development process, as these uses do not create new water demand on the system.

Mayor Vrbanovic emphasized that while broader water‑capacity solutions continue to be developed at the regional level, City staff have kept development applications moving in the background. He added that Kitchener staff are taking a proactive approach to maintain clear and consistent communication with residents, the development community, and all City partners in the coming weeks and months.

He also highlighted a recent decision by Regional Council to permanently allocate 30 L/s of new capacity to the Mannheim Service Area by rescinding the 1980 Wilmot Policy. He acknowledged that Council is aware of concerns raised by some Wilmot residents and recognizes the importance of respecting local communities and groundwater sustainability. The decision was guided by evidence, long‑term monitoring data, and responsible planning practices that support regional growth while protecting shared water resources. Mayor Vrbanovic stated he will continue advocating at the Region to ensure Kitchener’s priorities remain central.

Mayor Vrbanovic also reminded residents that those wishing to recycle their green bins may do so on April 19, 2026, at the Stanley Park Community Centre. However, where possible, residents are encouraged to keep and repurpose their bins for yard waste.

motions.item_title: Governance Review - Terms of Reference for Advisory Committees, COR-2026-131
motions.text: "That the Terms of References attached as Appendix A to Corporate Services Department report COR-2026-131 be approved, amended and repealed, effective November 15, 2026; and, That the revisions to the Appointments to Boards and Committee Policy (GOV-BOA-063) and the Honorarium and Reimbursement for Advisory Committee and Quasi-Judicial Committees of Council (GOV-BOA-2037), attached as Appendix B to Corporate Services Department report COR-2026-131 be approved; and further, That staff be directed to report back in 2027 in accordance with Corporate Services Department report COR-2026-131, on recommendations to modernize the traditional advisory committee model, considering emerging models that address engagement principles, and reduce duplication with existing processes."

motions.item_title: Rental Renovation Licensing By-law, COR-2026-045
Notice of Motion - S. Stretch - Localized Traffic Impacts at Victoria St N and Ahrens St W
motions.text: "That the following motion be deferred to the Special Council meeting on Monday April 20, 2026 : "WHEREAS localized traffic impacts are being experienced along Victoria Street North at Ahrens Street West during train arrival and departure times at the existing Kitchener Go/VIA station; WHEREAS Region of Waterloo staff have acknowledged that the Region is responsible for sidewalk snow clearing along the Regional and Metrolinx properties on Victoria Street; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed work with Regional Staff to review temporary and permanent modifications to the signalized intersection at Victoria Street North and Ahrens Street West, including but not limited to potential left turn restrictions and stop bar placement to improve traffic flow and intersection operations; and, THEREFORE BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED that staff be directed to work with Regional Staff to improve winter maintenance along the Regional and Metrolinx properties prior to Winter 2026."
motions.text_html:
"That the following motion be deferred to the Special Council meeting on Monday April 20, 2026:

"WHEREAS localized traffic impacts are being experienced along Victoria Street North at Ahrens Street West during train arrival and departure times at the existing Kitchener Go/VIA station;

WHEREAS Region of Waterloo staff have acknowledged that the Region is responsible for sidewalk snow clearing along the Regional and Metrolinx properties on Victoria Street; 

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed work with Regional Staff to review temporary and permanent modifications to the signalized intersection at Victoria Street North and Ahrens Street West, including but not limited to potential left turn restrictions and stop bar placement to improve traffic flow and intersection operations; and,

THEREFORE BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED that staff be directed to work with Regional Staff to improve winter maintenance along the Regional and Metrolinx properties prior to Winter 2026."

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - S. Stretch - Community Communications Plan around Transit Hub and GO Expansion
motions.text: "That the following motion be deferred to the Special Council meeting on Monday April 20, 2026: "WHEREAS improved local and inter-regional transit provides an overall net benefit for Kitchener residents; WHEREAS Progress toward dedicated GO rail service on the Kitchener Line is underway following a 2025 agreement in principle with CN, alongside recent service enhancements, including 18 new weekend trips and the first ever weekend service to Kitchener; WHEREAS construction of the Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH) and GO Expansion will be a multi-year project and will have multi-year localized community impacts during construction including, but not limited to noise, active transportation and traffic disruption and detours; WHEREAS The impact to the community immediately surrounding the build site and impacted by this construction should receive honest and direct communication; WHEREAS proactive project updates and communication are important factors in ensuring residents, businesses, neighbourhood associations and elected officials are informed during significant capital construction projects; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed to coordinate with the Region of Waterloo and Metrolinx on a communications plan and to set community meetings before 2027 and ongoing to inform and connect with residents, businesses, neighbourhood associations and elected officials throughout the multi-year construction process."
motions.text_html:
"That the following motion be deferred to the Special Council meeting on Monday April 20, 2026:

"WHEREAS improved local and inter-regional transit provides an overall net benefit for Kitchener residents;

WHEREAS Progress toward dedicated GO rail service on the Kitchener Line is underway following a 2025 agreement in principle with CN, alongside recent service enhancements, including 18 new weekend trips and the first ever weekend service to Kitchener; 

WHEREAS construction of the Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH) and GO Expansion will be a multi-year project and will have multi-year localized community impacts during construction including, but not limited to noise, active transportation and traffic disruption and detours;

WHEREAS The impact to the community immediately surrounding the build site and impacted by this construction should receive honest and direct communication;

WHEREAS proactive project updates and communication are important factors in ensuring residents, businesses, neighbourhood associations and elected officials are informed during significant capital construction projects;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed to coordinate with the Region of Waterloo and Metrolinx on a communications plan and to set community meetings before 2027 and ongoing to inform and connect with residents, businesses, neighbourhood associations and elected officials throughout the multi-year construction process."
